title: deployment-governance-1on1-scratchpad
body:
Context / purpose:
- Quick prep for my 1:1 with Evelyn (engineering lead) focused on Deployment Governance and short-term follow-ups across API/Console/Dedicated/Private.
- Goal: surface risks for Private rollout, decide on a narrow set of guardrails, and get concrete owners + dates.

High-level topics to cover (30m total):
1) Private deployment readiness: blockers + acceptance criteria (10m)
   - Security review status: where are we on KMS integration and audit log schema?
   - Networking checklist: VPC peering templates, default subnet guidance, cross-account IAM roles.
   - Minimum viable support matrix for first 3 customers (regions, GPU families, size).

2) Console UX for on-prem onboarding & rollout controls (8m)
   - Quick UX asks from sales: "one-click" invites vs manual token provisioning.
   - Rollout: canary toggles, model pinning UI, and per-tenant fallback policies.
   - Observability: what console panels do we expose by default for private installs (token-level cost is not available in private; what replaces it?).

3) Dedicated capacity autoscale + predictable SLOs (6m)
   - Autoscale policy: keep burst buffer but enforce per-tenant hard limits.
   - KPIs: P95 latency SLA target (in tokens/ms), throughput guarantees.

4) Open items + decisions I need from you (6m)
   - Decide on gating criteria to move a customer from pilot -> production for Private.
   - Approve temporary fallback policy for model mismatch during scale events.
   - Assign who will lead the KMS/HSM test plan.

Notes / talking points (talking order + quick scripts):
- Start: "High level ask — align on 3 guardrails we can commit to for next 6 weeks so we can greenlight 2 pilot customers."
- Private readiness: call out that legal sign-off for SOC has a dependency on audit log completeness; engineering needs 2 weeks to scope the missing fields. Ask: can we push legal for one-week extension?
- Console: UX team pushed a simplified onboarding flow but it omits per-tenant fallback settings. Suggest compromise: keep simplified flow but expose advanced toggle in Settings.
- Dedicated: mention the recent SRE findings about autoscale jitter causing QPS spikes; propose a soft cap mechanism and an emergency capacity pool.

Open risks I want on Evelyn's radar:
- Risk A: KMS/HSM integration unknowns — if we hit hardware HSM provisioning delays, Private installs may stall. Mitigation: a software KMS shim for pilot customers.
- Risk B: Observability gaps — no token-level cost in Private; sales will push for per-route cost estimates. Mitigation: provide sampled token metrics + cost-estimate dashboard based on model and batch size.
- Risk C: Customer-specific model variants — drift in model compatibility between hosted model catalog and private pinned models. Mitigation: compatibility test suite + automatic fallback mapping.

Draft acceptance criteria for pilot -> production (proposal):
- Security: KMS integration validated, audit logs include request id, model id, timestamp, and user id for >= 95% of calls.
- Networking: deployment playbook tested in at least 2 distinct customer VPC topologies.
- Performance: baseline P95 latency within 15% of equivalent hosted config for the same model family at typical sequence lengths.
- Observability: console shows per-route latency + error rates; sampling for token-level cost estimates available.

Proposed owners + short tasks (concrete, timeboxed):
- Evelyn: approve gating criteria + assign test lead for KMS (due: 2024-11-21).
- Kai: prototype software KMS shim for pilots, collab with security (due: 2024-11-28).
- Sam (me): consolidate pilot checklists, create "pilot readiness" Confluence page and coordinate sales legal ask (due: 2024-11-15).
- Observability lead (TBD): draft sampling config for token metrics and a mock dashboard (due: 2024-11-25).

Quick follow-ups I will send after the 1:1:
- Email thread to SRE + Security summarizing agreed guardrails + owners.
- Create INF ticket for "KMS pilot shim" and add Kai as assignee.
- Update Confluence pilot page with acceptance criteria and test matrix.

Potential yes/no asks to surface during the meeting:
- Approve temporary software KMS shim for pilot customers (yes/no).
- Allow console simplified onboarding to roll to beta while keeping advanced settings hidden behind a feature flag (yes/no).
- Greenlight reallocation of $X of dedicated capacity to build emergency pool for autoscale jitter (yes/no).

Other background snippets to reference (short):
- Sales note: two pilots expected (EU-regulated fintech, on-prem healthcare). Fintech requires HSM-backed KMS; healthcare can accept software shim for now.
- SRE note: jitter typically spikes during training window alignment; investigated kernel-level scheduling but short-term mitigation is config-level.
- UX note: sales prefers "invite by email" for onboarding; security prefers pre-provisioned service accounts for audits. Need middle ground.

Meeting checklist (what I will bring):
- One-pager with proposed gating criteria (PDF)
- Link to pilot Confluence (will create before meeting)
- Short list of potential fallback models for compatibility mapping

Post-meeting template (to copy into follow-up email):
- Subject: 1:1 recap — Deployment guardrails + owners
- Body: brief bullets with decisions, owners, and due dates, plus ask for any objections within 48h.

Loose notes / stream-of-consciousness (scratch):
- Consider making a "pilot health" badge visible to Sales in console so they can self-check readiness before asking for GA. Could be just a pass/fail checklist instead of live telemetry.
- If HSM provisioning is frequent blocker, consider standard partner for HSM quick-provisioning. Log as long-term ops project.
- Need to define what "production" means in the Private context (is it SLA-backed or just customer-acknowledged production?).

End of notes.
